scenes.title: Fit is a practical question
scenes.visual: Founder reviews opportunity and calendar cards.
scenes.narration: An opportunity may sound useful, but is it a sensible next learning focus for you now? Founder fit means access, capability, resources and commitment for the next step. It is not a personality test or proof of business success. Separate the opportunity’s evidence from your enthusiasm.

scenes.title: Assess importance and alternatives
scenes.visual: Editable importance and current approach cards.
scenes.narration: How important might the problem be for the specific group, and what evidence supports that view? Include what existing approaches do well. Keep frequency, consequences and willingness to change unknown when unsupported. A strong-sounding value proposition is still a hypothesis.

scenes.title: Check access and capability
scenes.visual: Founder maps a task to a skill or support route.
scenes.narration: Can you ethically reach relevant people and sources? Can you perform the next check with your current skills or appropriate help? Distinguish demonstrated capability from a plan to learn or find support. Pending permission is not access, and a named contact is not a confirmed commitment.

scenes.title: Respect resources and constraints
scenes.visual: Editable time, budget, permission and dependency cards.
scenes.narration: Use your realistic time, budget and commitment from earlier lessons. Identify dependencies, privacy or permission limits and what would stop the next step. Fit can improve through learning, support or a narrower scope. A weak fit today does not mean you are not a founder.

scenes.title: Use ratings without false precision
scenes.visual: Editable Low, Medium, High and Unknown cards.
scenes.narration: You may use low, medium, high or unknown as provisional judgments for importance, access and capability. Rate uncertainty separately; high uncertainty means more is unresolved. Explain each rating with evidence and limits. Do not add them into a success score or let a number override a critical constraint.

scenes.title: Choose a bounded next action
scenes.narration: Create your Opportunity and Founder Fit Assessment. Record judgments, evidence, resources, gaps and critical constraints. Choose to explore further, narrow, seek support or pause, with a next check and review trigger. This is a learning decision, not venture approval or a prediction of success.

sections.label: 02 / LEARN
sections.heading: Assess the opportunity and your next-step fit separately.

children: Opportunity assessment
asks whether the problem and proposed improvement merit further investigation.
Founder fit
asks whether you can realistically perform the next learning step, with access, skills, support and resources. Neither predicts venture success.
Importance
Does the difficulty matter to the specific group? Preserve evidence and what current approaches already solve.
Reachability
Can you ethically reach relevant people or sources? Pending permission is not confirmed access.
Capability
Can you perform the next check? Separate demonstrated skills, learning plans and unconfirmed support.
Uncertainty
What remains unresolved? High uncertainty means more unknowns, not a high success score.
Use a reasoned rating
For importance, access and capability, use
Low / Medium / High / Unknown
if helpful, followed by evidence, limits and a next check. Rate uncertainty separately. These are self-judgments, not measured scores. No total or automatic recommendation is calculated.

Critical constraints matter independently: missing permission, inadequate time or an unsafe method can block the next step even when other judgments look positive. Fit can improve by narrowing the scope, learning or securing confirmed help.
Illustrative example:

a founder with venue experience may have relevant skills, but access remains pending until permission is confirmed. A feasible desk-based source check could be a fallback. This does not prove demand or business viability.
Choose a bounded action

Explore further, narrow the question, seek support or pause. Explain why, state the next check and set a review trigger. Pausing can be a reasonable decision; it is not a judgment of your identity or worth.
Review skills & support
Review commitment plan
Review opportunity statement
Review value proposition
